definitions.explanation: Emphasizes that something happens only once and cannot be repeated, often carrying a sense of preciousness or urgency about a unique opportunity.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}は{一度|いちど}きりだ。
そのチャンスは{一度|いちど}きりだった。
{一度|いちど}きりの{出会|であ}いを{大切|たいせつ}にしたい。
examples.english: I want to cherish this one-time encounter.

notes:
An expression emphasizing that something happens only once and cannot be repeated. Combines {一度|いちど} (once) with きり (only, nothing more). Often carries a sense of preciousness or urgency — the one chance should not be wasted.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {人生|じんせい}は{一度|いちど}きり: you only live once
- {一度|いちど}きりの{体験|たいけん}: a once-in-a-lifetime experience
- {一度|いちど}きりしかない: there is only one chance

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一回|いっかい}きり — same meaning but slightly more casual
- たった{一度|いちど} — emphasizes "just once" with a different nuance of smallness
- {二度|にど}とない — never again; emphasizes irreversibility
